claim: For every integer \(m\ge 4\), let \(\Theta_m\) be the graph with two vertices joined by \(m\) parallel edges, let \(B_3(\Theta_m)\) be the unordered configuration space of three points, and let \(A_m=\ker(\mathbb Z^m\xrightarrow{\sum}\mathbb Z)\) be the edge augmentation lattice. Permuting edges gives \(S_m\)-actions, and \(H_2(B_3(\Theta_m);\mathbb Z)\cong\bigwedge^3 A_m\) equivariantly. Under a consistent orientation, the theta class on ordered distinct edges \(i,j,k,l\) maps to \((e_j-e_i)\wedge(e_k-e_i)\wedge(e_l-e_i)\). Hence the theta classes containing any fixed edge form an integral basis, and all integral relations among oriented four-edge theta classes are generated by the five-term boundary relations on five distinct edges.

correctness.rationale: Exploding one essential vertex of \(\Theta_m\) gives the \(m\)-armed star. Its reduced Świątkowski complex is the two-term complex \(R\otimes A_m\to R\), with \(d(a_i)=x_i=e_i-e_0\). Thus degree-two homology of the star vanishes. In weight \(2\), the first homology is \(\bigwedge^2 A_m\); in weight \(3\), the kernel in the vertex-explosion sequence is exactly the image of the injective Koszul map \(\bigwedge^3 A_m\to A_m\otimes\bigwedge^2A_m\). Naturality identifies each four-edge theta class with the displayed exterior wedge. Fixed-edge theta classes map to an exterior basis, and exterior expansion gives and generates the five-term relations. The finite verifier independently checks the coordinate and relation matrices for \(4\le m\le10\) in several characteristics.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a numerical Betti count to a natural integral representation of the full edge-permutation symmetry and supplies a complete relation mechanism for the embedded theta generators. It clarifies how the many four-edge theta subgraphs interact as \(m\) grows, beyond generation-only and Euler-characteristic descriptions. The fixed-edge basis and five-term relations are reusable in functorial and representation-theoretic calculations. The primary source explicitly poses universal degree-two relations and combinatorial bases as open questions; this theorem resolves both on the generalized-theta, three-particle slice.
